summary: Father Andrew discusses the accusation that Orthodox Christians practice idolatry by venerating icons, referencing the Seventh Ecumenical Council held in Nicaea in 787. He explains that the Council Fathers argued that because God became incarnate in Jesus Christ, depicting Him honors the reality of the Incarnation rather than worshipping the material object. The speaker concludes that veneration directed at icons or the Eucharist is ultimately given to the divine presence within them, affirming that denying the Incarnation denies Christianity itself.
